nullishStrippedByAssertion.text: This assertion removes `undefined` or `null` from the value's type without a check, the same claim a `!` makes. From here on the type says the value is present, so the compiler stops asking, and a fallback after it (`?? fallback`) reads as dead code. Fix it in this order. If the value can really be missing, guard it: check it first, or keep `| undefined` in the asserted type and handle it, so the missing case has code. If it cannot, fix the type that says it can, so there is no claim left to check; a command-line flag reads through `stringFlag` or `numberFlag`, whose types are already honest. Where neither fits, state the proof with `required(value, 'why it is present')` from `@nexus/source/errors/Assert`, which narrows the same way and throws that sentence if the proof is ever wrong.

forceCast.text: as! crashes the process when the value is not that type. Use as? and say what happens when it is not.
